contact_edits.before: The staging goes against the published script in denying us a proper look at the painting, which is a loss since its subject -- Mary mourning the dead Jesus -- is as important as its provenance. Someone in the play describes Marxism as a good idea that hasn't been tried; the same of course has been said of Christianity. The play wants, I think, to harvest the most humane elements of both while lamenting the improbability. It calls to mind George Orwell's description of Dickens: "generously angry." It's a genuinely inspiring evening. - Pentecost is in repertoire until Sept. 21. Call 1-800-567-1600 for ticket information.
